page: Amazon Web Services m8ib.48xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose Nitro instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by dedicated Intel processors running at 3.9 GHz, delivering 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 768.0 GB, which preserves the standard general-purpose allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Networking performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 200 Gbps provided through the AWS Nitro hypervisor subsystem. The platform does not bundle local storage, necessitating reliance on remote block storage solutions such as Amazon EBS for persistent data. The instance provision also excludes complimentary public IPv4 addressing, operating within virtual private network boundaries.

Given the balanced memory-to-compute ratio alongside dense core counts and 200 Gbps connectivity, the instance is positioned for large enterprise workloads that require high networking throughput and parallel compute capacity. Common operational fits include large-scale web backends, distributed data pipelines, enterprise application servers, in-memory caching systems, and high-concurrency microservice architectures.

This hardware footprint provides substantial compute density and data throughput without local drive overhead, positioning the m8ib.48xlarge for network-heavy microservice platforms, large enterprise database engines, multi-threaded backend batch processing, and distributed analytics pipelines.
